BiblicalUsage: Smoky is used twice, for the mountain and for the firebrands. The people see the thunderings and the lightnings and the mountain smoking, and stand afar off; and Isaiah tells Ahaz not to fear the two tails of smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin and of the son of Remaliah.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for smoky carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that the mountain smokes with God's presence, and the kings who threaten Judah are only smoking ends, already going out.
